headline: Notion AI Agents are live with external data sync and custom code via Workers
summary: Notion has launched Custom Agents, Workers for custom code and data sync, and External Agents for third-party AI, transforming it into an AI-powered operating layer. These features are live and free to try on Business/Enterprise plans.
details: Notion has rolled out a suite of AI agent capabilities, including Custom Agents, a developer platform with "Workers," and External Agents. These features, launched throughout 2026, are currently live and available for trial on Business and Enterprise plans.

Custom Agents, launched in February 2026, handle repetitive knowledge-work tasks within a Notion workspace. While over a million were built, the first wave lacked external data connections and custom logic capabilities.

Notion addressed these limitations on May 13, 2026, with its developer platform featuring "Workers." This hosted runtime allows teams to deploy custom code for data syncing, exposing new tools to agents, and responding to webhooks without managing their own servers.

Powered by Workers, Database Sync pulls live records from external systems like Salesforce, Zendesk, or Postgres directly into Notion databases. This integration makes Notion agents genuinely useful for operational work beyond just drafting text.

On July 1, 2026, Notion 3.6 introduced External Agents, allowing integration of AI from Claude, Cursor, and others, assignable tasks, and mentions within the workspace. This release also added interactive HTML blocks, speaker-labeled AI meeting notes, and native Microsoft Office file support.

Notion's strategy is to become the central hub where teams and AI agents collaborate, rather than just another app. This positions it as a knowledge-work orchestration layer, offering cross-functional visibility and aiding judgment-in-the-loop tasks.

While traditional workflow automation platforms focus on reliable data movement between systems, Notion excels at providing a shared surface for people and agents to see state and act on assembled data. It aims to do both, but is stronger in the latter.

headline_marked: [[Cerebras CS-4 is the fastest AI accelerator]] in the industry, delivering up to 30x faster inference
headline: Cerebras CS-4 is the fastest AI accelerator in the industry, delivering up to 30x faster inference
summary: Cerebras CS-4, powered by WSE-Turbo, offers up to 30x faster AI inference than GPU systems. This rack-scale solution also provides enhanced economics and simplified hyperscale deployment.
details: Cerebras has introduced the CS-4, a new rack-scale AI accelerator designed for frontier AI. It delivers up to 30x faster inference compared to GPU systems, setting a new record for production inference speed.
The CS-4 is powered by the WSE-Turbo, with each wafer offering up to twice the speed of the previous generation. New power, cooling, and I/O systems further enhance performance per wafer.

This solution shifts the inference Pareto frontier, achieving up to 10x more throughput per watt than the CS-3. It also generates tokens up to 30x faster than current production GPU systems, balancing both throughput and interactivity.

By reducing wafer-to-wafer interconnect latency to just 2 microseconds, the CS-4 can deliver over 1,000 tokens per second. This performance is maintained even on models exceeding 10 trillion parameters, ensuring interactive decode performance at unprecedented scale.

The CS-4 is the first iteration of the new Cerebras Nexus Platform Architecture, built on a modular concept. It features three foundational elements: Compute, Power, and I/O, each with significant innovations for simplified manufacturing, deployment, maintenance, and upgrades.

The Wafer-Scale Backpack is a self-contained assembly that integrates the wafer, power conversion, direct liquid cooling, high-speed I/O, and control electronics into a compact 3D package. This design reduces component count by 50% and cuts deployment time from days to hours.

Power delivery is just 0.5 millimeters from the processor, approximately 100x closer than conventional GPU boards. This proximity nearly eliminates board-level power loss, allowing twice as much power to the WSE-3T for higher operating frequencies and faster token generation.

A new programmable I/O subsystem doubles I/O bandwidth and reduces latency, benefiting both aggregated and disaggregated solutions. The Wafer I/O Module enables wafers to be linked within and across racks without a switch, achieving wafer-to-wafer latency as low as two microseconds for large models.

The Cerebras PowerRack separates the stable power, cooling, and network layer from the modular wafer-scale compute. This allows the PowerRack to be installed and qualified before compute arrives, simplifying service and future upgrades at hyperscale by reducing deployment from days to hours.
